item.title: Laid Off by Email, She Bought a One-Way Ticket to Bali and Built a Studio From a Rented Room | A Relaxing Story
item.description:
The email that ended eleven years of Grace Bowen's life arrived at 9.02 on a Monday, and by the second paragraph she already knew her name was on it.
Grace Bowen designed for a Seattle tech company for eleven years, until a Monday email cut her whole team. She spent her severance on a one-way ticket to Canggu, Bali, and turned a rented room and a laptop into a branding studio for the island's cafes and surf brands. A complete, relaxing story about being erased at thirty-nine, backing herself when nobody else will, and building a life and a business from nothing in a town full of people who all left something behind. item.title: She Quit Fast Furniture to Build Mahogany by Hand in Barbados | A Relaxing Story
item.description:
For eight years her job was deciding exactly how long a chair was allowed to live, twenty four months and not one more, until a dusty shuttered workshop on a Caribbean island asked her a question she could not fly home from, and answering it cost her the job, the apartment, and every plan she had, and gave her back her hands.
Ellie Brandt spent eight years in Seattle engineering chairs to survive exactly as long as their warranty and not a day longer. On a family trip to Barbados she wandered into a shuttered workshop that once made the island's great mahogany furniture, the tools still hanging on the wall under dust, and she could not stop thinking about it. She went back alone, leased the workshop, and learned real joinery from the retired master who once ran it, working only with storm-fallen and replanted mahogany. item.title: She Flew to Vietnam to Buy Pearls Cheap. She Quit Her Job to Stop It Instead | A Relaxing Story
item.description:
Laura Kessler had flown to Vietnam to put her signature on a deal that would save her company nine dollars a pearl, and she was about to spend the next year making sure that signature never happened.
Laura Kessler spent fourteen years sourcing gemstones for a US jewelry chain. Her company sent her to Duong Dong, Phu Quoc, to lock in a cheap bulk pearl deal that would have rushed the harvest and ruined the oysters. She met the widow keeping the farm alive, saw exactly what the deal would do to it, and quit rather than sign it. A complete, relaxing story about walking away from a good job to help build a better one, on the real river town of Duong Dong, Phu Quoc, Vietnam. Names, characters, and the pearl farm are fictional.
